what: Flat firmware images recovered from the vendor SDL upgrade packages in docs/usrdl/, and the comparison showing the Sportster Vi DSVD firmware to be a cut-down Courier
sources: docs/usrdl/dsvd-sdl.exe, sdl_61.exe, usrsdl.exe - vendor archives, tracked in this repository

carriers.sdl-loader: DOS SDL*.EXE embed the image as 16-byte binary download records: [len=0x10][addr hi][addr lo][type=00][16 data][checksum], record summing to zero mod 256
carriers.xmd: 64-byte header, then the image under a flat XOR 0x55

format_evidence: The checksum identifies the record format rather than a pattern coincidence: 13193 consecutive records validate in SDL.EXE, 15396 in SDL_7666.EXE, 18090 in SDL20.EXE

result.identical_structures: ATI7 field layout, the product-name table carrying both Courier and Sportster, the result-code table in the same order
result.removed_from_sportster: HST result codes, Dial Security, Remote Access, dipswitch display, serial number, ASL statistics, developer credits
result.added_in_sportster: DSVD voice path - AUDIO date/rev, Audio Sampling Rate, Algorithm Selection, Blocking Factor, -SMUTE, -SMUX
result.dating: Sportster copyright ends 1993, Courier 7666 ends 1995, Sportster package dated 12/95 - a 1993 fork maintained separately

limits: The recovered images are NOT flash-accurate. Record addresses are 16 bits and wrap, so they order records within a segment but do not place them in a 512 KiB flash. Segment breaks are reported, not resolved: 17 in the Sportster loader, 23 in SDL_7666, 27 in SDL20. Nothing here should be handed to the emulator as a flash image.
The 64-byte XMD header is not decoded. It varies per build around an NHCFG marker; a checksum and a model gate are plausible and untested.
The comparison is string-level only. No code was disassembled and no entry points were matched, so 'cut-down Courier' rests on shared data tables and layout, not on identical instruction sequences.
INT80188 in SDL_7666.EXE versus INT80186 in SDL20.EXE is a string read out of the images, not a part checked against a board.
